AI Twitter Recap 
GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol 
Availability. Today’s models are rolling out to ChatGPT Work and Codex for Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu, and to developers through the API as gpt-6.2-astra and gpt-6.2-sol . OpenAI 
API prices per million tokens. Astra is $8 input, $0.40 cached input and $40 output. Sol keeps its predecessor’s pricing at $2, $0.10 and $10. Both have 1M context and a 128K output limit. Vals · Ultrafast pricing and rollout 
Astra for Law. The Enterprise configuration adds a legal search index. Artificial Analysis measured 20.8% on Harvey LAB-AA, versus 15.0% for base Astra. Artificial Analysis 
Preparedness. OpenAI rated Astra High for AI Self-Improvement, a first for one of its externally released models. On a separate measure, Vals’ RSI-Index rose from 27.07% to 29.01%, with 50% denoting its human reference. System card · Vals 
FrontierMath Erdős. Epoch verified seven solutions in Lean out of 68 problems. The previous best was three. Epoch 
What the benchmarks measure 
Agents’ Last Exam 1.1. OpenAI reports Astra at xhigh gained 5.2 points over GPT-6 Astra at max, using less than a third of the cost per task. It reports a 5.5-point lead over Fable 5.2 at about 5% of the cost on that test. On GDPval v2, it says Astra used 22% fewer output tokens than its predecessor. OpenAI’s results 
Long engineering runs. Mercor’s OpenWorldEngineer puts Astra at 67.2%, Fable 5.2 at 54.6%, and GPT-6 Astra at 44.2%. On Vals’ multi-turn Vibe Code Bench, Astra was first and Sol was third. Mercor · Vals 
3D and robotics. Astra led AA-3D with 1,318, ahead of Fable at 1,271 and Sol at 1,259. On Artificial Analysis’s robotics preview, Astra scored 79 and Sol 78, ahead of Fable at 75. Artificial Analysis 
Research agents. On Perplexity’s WANDR, Astra scored 0.783 at about $12.54 per task. Sol reached 0.746 at about $2.65. Perplexity 
Early testers disagreed 
Matt Shumer called the models “essentially unusable” after weeks of testing and said his Opus and Fable agents rejected much of Astra’s subagent work. Review · Workflow details 
Pietro Schirano attributed many of his early issues to the harness. Arena’s Peter Gostev tested Astra against Fable on visual coding and singled out Astra’s SVG peacock. Schirano · Gostev 
The demos. Gabriel Chua built a walkable Singapore using more than 100 Codex threads. Simon Willison ran the same three.js mech prompt through several models, including Astra, Sol, Carbon and Fable. Singapore build · Same-prompt comparison

business@latent.space → 
Microsoft Ignite and Gemini 
Microsoft ships its own coding models. MAI Code 2 is for multi-step coding, and Code 2 Flash is for quicker edits. Both are available in GitHub Copilot’s model picker, Copilot Fusion and Foundry. Microsoft also announced a multimodal upgrade to its Decision model. Microsoft 
Copilot Fusion. Microsoft reports 71.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.1 with its multi-model harness, at 88% lower cost than Claude Fable 5.2 in that comparison. Jay Parikh 
Image editing. Artificial Analysis ranks MAI Image 2.7 first on its editing benchmark, at $34.82 per 1,000 images. Artificial Analysis 
Gemini Tasks. Hydrogen now powers free Tasks in six countries, including tasks that need a phone call or a text. Google also showed a new Antigravity robotics plugin with MuJoCo simulation. Sundar Pichai · Google DeepMind 
Agent harnesses and inference 
Hugging Face’s Pi adapter. A small adapter trained inside pi lifted Qwen3.8-27B from 15 to 32 solves on the 51 hardest SWE-bench Pro tasks. Across that subset it made 55% fewer tool calls per task. Model card and paired results 
Harness costs vary sharply. Baseten measured up to a 4.4× spread in cost per passing task across its benchmark of 22 harnesses and five open models. Baseten 
The harness may specialize to its model. Google’s SIM keeps the rationale and outcome of prior harness edits. A harness it evolved on Opus scored 68.41 on Gemini, versus 73.89 for the starting harness. Research summary 
More multi-agent products. Cognition launched persistent Devin Bots. Perplexity reported that its mixed-model teams beat four instances of the lead model on Terminal-Bench and WANDR. Replit reported diminishing returns from 16 to 32 agents on NumPy tasks. Cognition · Perplexity · Replit 
Coordination dominated a 1,000-agent run. Hugging Face says only 40–60 agents were calling the model at any moment. They read roughly 130 tokens for every token they wrote, with merges and tests contributing to the bottleneck. Thomas Wolf 
A small fraction of cache misses can dominate the bill. SemiAnalysis reports that 1.8% of uncached requests accounted for roughly 15% of spend in its sample. SemiAnalysis 
Marin and K2 Horizon opened up their training runs. Marin released 57 intermediate Mochi checkpoints from its 535B-A23B run. The K2 report compares four model sizes trained on the same 22T tokens and describes a decoding adapter that the team says reaches 2.2× speedup. Marin · K2 Horizon 
Zyphra’s long-context attention. The team reports 9–60× speedups at 10M tokens after converting several models to its subquadratic attention, with Qwen losing under two points on RULER at 1M. Zyphra 
Speculative decoding. vLLM reports up to 30% higher acceptance length from a sliding-window draft for Kimi K3.1 Pro. NVIDIA also has a 4B draft for Qwen3.8-27B. vLLM · Draft-model research 
Industry and policy 
NVIDIA’s first earnings after the CEO transition. Under interim CEO Colette Kress, NVIDIA posted $115.8B in quarterly revenue, up 103% year over year, and said Vera Rubin NVL72 had shipped. The board said it did not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang. NVIDIA · AP 
Isomorphic Labs raises $5B. Greenoaks and Sequoia co-led the Series C. The company says it will scale its drug-design platform and develop its therapeutic pipeline. Isomorphic Labs 
Genesis AI raises $500M. The Series A values the robotics company at $3.5B post-money. It plans to use the funding to deploy its Eno robot and expand training and data collection. Zhou Xian 
AI Reddit Recap 
Local models and hardware 
A 9B model with layers that run twice. SenseNova-Loop-9B runs 24 of its 32 layers a second time. The model’s authors report GAIA rising from 37.86 in the preview to 69.90 in the release. Local users asked how much memory remains for the KV cache at long context. Weights · Discussion 
Maxwell V1 Flash. The 35B/3B-active MoE claims a 6.7× attention speedup over dense GQA at 256K. Its sparse attention still retains the full-history KV cache, which is what local users want measured before they commit hardware. Model card · Discussion 
Olala mini 7A1B. OVHcloud previewed a small MoE with 1B active parameters and a 32K context window. The thread is waiting for weights and reproducible benchmarks. OVHcloud · Discussion 
Intel’s Crescent Island numbers. The early brief’s eye-catching throughput comparison uses FP64-heavy workloads. Intel’s separate LLM comparison claims 1.12× throughput and 29% lower latency versus RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition. Hardware discussion 
Gemma on a printer. A builder reports running Gemma 3 270M via a PostScript print job. Demo 
Agents in use 
A video-game agent built for real-time input. miHoYo’s Gamer samples the screen at 5 Hz and emits keyboard and mouse activity at 30 Hz. Its RL version solved about half of the held-out Honkai puzzle tasks in the authors’ evaluation. Project · Discussion 
A fictional league runs a nightly broadcast. The builder says Fock Ball simulates the games in a physics engine and uses Claude for surrounding work such as commentary and the newsroom. Builder’s post 
ICLR reviews and AI detectors. Reviewers report that the program chairs flagged likely AI-generated reviews. The thread asks how a detector can distinguish editing help from whole-review generation. Peer review discussion

Jensen is out. Who should run NVIDIA next?

“It has to be an external CEO, given all of the questions around chip shipments to China. I hope it is Charlie Kawwas of Broadcom or Johny Srouji of Apple.”

“If it is internal candidates, Ian Buck and Jonah Alben are the two best bets. But everything around shipping chips to China is going to be very, very scrutinized. Did they know? What did they know?”

“Jensen has been the defender of open source. Now there is no one defending Chinese open source anymore. Certainly the restrictions from the US on China are about to ramp up.”

Cloudflare Joins the Jevolution and Labels Itself a Neolab 
Cloudflare made its name speeding up the web. Now it's building System One models to make decisions and pull data in milliseconds. 
Richard MacManus 
Nov 17 · 6 min read
On this page ⌄ What is a neolab and is Cloudflare really one? Jev as the “east wind” Clairic and what extraction models do Why Cloudflare is in the lab now 
Cloudflare has been one of the essential infrastructure companies of the web for the past decade and a half. But now, it’s turning into a neolab — at least according to a presentation at AI Engineer Code Summit by Michelle Chen , who runs Cloudflare’s AI Platform on the product side. 
We’ll get into what exactly a neolab is in a minute (the short version: they build models and they’re not called OpenAI or Anthropic). Cloudflare is claiming to be one because it too has begun to launch models. Two System One models , to be precise: Clef and Clairic. As Chen explained in her talk, Clef is a decision model directly inspired by TypeSafe AI’s revolutionary Jev model , while Clairic is a new type of system one model that Cloudflare calls an “extract” model . 
In an interview with Latent Space after her presentation, Chen hinted that Cloudflare won’t just be producing system one models. There will be large language models, too. 
“We're not being a neolab [to] only launch system one models, even though it makes sense for our infrastructure. We've kind of entered this Pandora's box now, right? We opened it, now the possibilities are endless.” 
Chen said it’s “not just system one models, but potentially reasoning models that we've been experimenting with, and other LLMs and whatnot.”  
However, she added that these probably won’t be pre-trained models built from scratch, like the frontier labs produce. 
“I don't think that's our focus, but I think we can take existing resources out there and make [them] a lot more efficient and effective.” 
She noted that “most of our team really just does post-training,” so that will be the focus in model development. 
What is a neolab and is Cloudflare really one? 
The term neolab literally means a ‘new lab’ and it was coined last November by Stephanie Palazzolo from The Information, who defined it as “a new generation of research-focused AI startups.” 
Deedy Das , a partner at Menlo Ventures and an AI influencer, runs a big list of neolabs . It includes companies like Thinking Machines Lab, Poolside, and TypeSafe AI itself. According to Das, neolabs employ elite researchers, spend a lot of compute (“usually to train its own AI model”), don't have significant revenue traction, and they’re typically startups that have raised a lot of money. 
Deedy Das’ list of neolabs — note that TypeSafe is among the top 20. 
Cloudflare doesn’t tick at least half of those boxes, since it’s a public company with significant revenue traction . In fact, earlier this month Cloudflare announced record earnings . “The third quarter was Cloudflare's best quarter ever,” said CEO Matthew Prince . “We crossed $3 billion in annualized revenue with revenue of $782 million, up 39% year over year.” 
So Cloudflare as a “neolab” is pushing the accepted definition. However, as Chen argued in her presentation, building models is part of a natural progression for the company : from infrastructure, to compute (e.g. the Workers platform, including now for agents), to storage, to serving open weight models like Kimi, GLM and DeepSeek (on Workers AI), to now building its own models. 
Jev as the “east wind”

Chen readily admits that Jev inspired Cloudflare’s pivot to building models. Referencing a Chinese proverb, she framed Jev’s arrival in September as “the east wind” that unexpectedly changed how Cloudflare viewed AI models. 
“And so when the system one and Jev paradigm started coming on board,” Chen said in her presentation, “we were like, this makes so much sense for us to adopt, right? We don't have to send every request to an LLM. We can send some of it to a System One model.” 
In our conversation, Chen commented on how it took only two weeks for them to build Clef — which is a copy of Jev — whereas it took TypeSafe AI two years to build Jev. She meant that as a compliment for how hard TypeSafe AI worked to create this new type of model. 
“All credit to TypeSafe, really, for actually attacking this space and inventing something new here , that people could relate to so strongly and be able to use it. And, yeah, we came up with a model super quickly, but they put in a lot of legwork and we knew exactly what the API schema should look like and whatnot.” 
Cloudflare is, at its core, still an infrastructure company — speed and low latency is its meat and potatoes. The main benefit of System One models, Chen remarked, is that they allow more work to be done by smaller, faster models , where output is measured in milliseconds rather than seconds. 
Clairic and what extraction models do 
While Clef was a clone of Jev, Cloudflare soon came up with an original twist on System One with Clairic , launched last month as “the first model in a new class: System One extraction models.” 
“What Clairic does is it can take unstructured input, and it can extract, compute, estimate and forecast values from those inputs,” Chen explained in her presentation. 
In our interview, Chen said that her team wanted to use System One principles to find other areas where LLMs were “overkill” and didn’t always return the right answer. 
One of the problems they settled on was that LLMs don’t always deal well with unstructured input. Because LLMs are autoregressive, Chen explained, they are prone to hallucinate and they sometimes return malformed JSON. 
“So we used the same System One principles [as Jev/Clef] there, and decided on extraction.” 
Some examples of system one use cases at Cloudflare. 
She used the example of an invoice, where an LLM will sometimes get an important detail wrong — like the order number. 
“When you send it [the order] to an LLM, they're like, wait, I think the order number's three, maybe it's four, maybe it's five. But it's like, the number's right there, you just have to read it! ” 
So the idea with Clairic is that it will extract a typed value — like a number — from unstructured data, in one forward pass. 
Why Cloudflare is in the lab now 
Using the label “neolab” sounds a bit like a marketing gimmick, but it also makes a ton of sense for Cloudflare to produce system one models — and even, in future, reasoning models.  
“Being a neolab means that we can create what we are missing,” Chen said in her presentation.  
In our interview, she also mentioned that creating their own models allows Cloudflare to derisk its AI operations. 
“I think there's a lot of risk in the AI space , because just like Jev was closed source and we couldn't run it, there [are] a lot of models out there [with] maybe regulatory risks coming up, like the Chinese open source models. I think lots of model labs want to actually make money, as well — so enforcing quite expensive licenses.” 
If you look at Cloudflare’s product page now, it resembles what Amazon’s cloud computing product page looked like at the height of Web 2.0 — i.e. there’s a lot there! 
But there’s still room for several more models.

podcasts.title: Brad Gerstner & Geoffrey Canada - Raising the Floor for Every American Child - [Invest Like the Best, EP.501]
podcasts.description:
My guests today are Brad Gerstner, founder of Altimeter Capital, and Geoffrey Canada, founder of Harlem Children's Zone. Geoffrey spent decades helping disadvantaged kids get a great education, but it takes more than that to achieve the American dream. Without savings, you’re one emergency away from bankruptcy.

Brad set out to change that. When he first called me about Invest America in 2020, I thought it was a fool’s errand. Six years later, nearly 70 million children have accounts in their name, and every American newborn receives $1,000 in the S&P 500. The challenge now is getting families to claim their accounts, since free money is surprisingly hard to give away.

Brad and Geoffrey believe even a small nest egg, when given a head start on compounding, can help rebuild faith in capitalism. As AI reshapes the economy, they see these accounts as the basis of a new social contract built on ownership and participation, where every child owns a piece of the upside.

Please enjoy my conversation with Brad and Geoffrey.

Perplexity hits a $1B revenue run rate, up 4x in 2026 
November 16, 2026 — Computer gets Teammates, Perplexity ships Monitor API, and a new research lab launches. 
swyx .ai 
Nov 17 · 9 min read
Perplexity crossed a $1B annual revenue run rate today , CEO Aravind Srinivas told Semafor at a live event. The Information reported previously under $250M at the start of the year and over $750M by August, with Computer driving some of the growth. At usual agent lab multiples (eg Cognition also crossed $1B , with Cursor crossing $4.6B ), this would roughly mean that Perplexity is now worth $30-50B — if the unit economics hold up. This is a nice bump on the $20B round in September 2025 , and qualifies for our “>$10B fundraise” rule for title stories. 
Gathering up some recent Perplexity launches for those catching up: 
Computer. September’s Automations let it pick up recurring tasks where it left off. November’s Teammates take on ongoing jobs. Computer also runs fully locally on supported Macs. 
Monitor API. Watch a topic or page and get a webhook when something relevant changes. 
Frontier Research. The new research lab has access to 10,000+ GPUs and plans to publish papers, data, models, and code. 
Sponsored by Deepgram 
Deepgram is the voice AI infrastructure behind natural conversation—bringing speech-to-text, text-to-speech, voice-focused LLMs, and agents to teams building with voice AI. For any stack and any tools you already love building with, Deepgram slots in as your foundational voice AI technology. So you have control. And we have the context to listen, understand, and speak like a human. 
Learn more about the Real-time Context Standard . 
AI Twitter Recap 
Qwen4-Max in the wild 
Friday’s Qwen4-Max preview is now a shipping model. At the highest reasoning setting, Qwen4-Max scored 43 on the Intelligence Index, up from 34. Average cost fell from $10.02 to $3.27 per task. Alibaba cut output pricing from $6 to $4.50 per million tokens, and the model generated about 39% fewer of them. Kimi K3.1 Pro cost $3.68 per index task and scored 67% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 to Qwen’s 48%. Artificial Analysis 
Inside the model. Alibaba kept the total parameter count at 2.4T and reduced the number active per token by 25% to 71B. The model takes images and text, with a 1M-token context window. Smaller open-weight Qwen4 models are still to come. Alibaba 
Arena and Vals : Arena ranks it #14 overall on Agent Arena, the top Chinese model, with +7.5% net over 14.7k sessions ( Arena ). 
WebDev : It placed #6 in Code Arena WebDev at 1750, +74 over its predecessor ( WebDev ). It also placed #6 in Image-to-WebDev, just above Claude Opus 5 and GPT-6 Sol ( I2WebDev ). 
Vals Index : It is #11 overall, with large gains in coding and finance ( Vals ). 
Legal-benchmark caveat : On HLAB it gets 95.7% of checklist items right but passes only 21.3% of tasks, and its output tokens rise 3.6x ( HLAB ). 
Vision results (independent) : Roboflow calls it underwhelming on its VLM benchmark, with Google, OpenAI and Anthropic now far ahead. At high reasoning effort, however, it is ~4.5x faster and ~68% cheaper per image than Qwen3.8-Max ( Roboflow ). 
Safety, alignment and eval integrity 
OpenAI embedded assessments : OpenAI is giving Apollo, METR, Transluce and Goodfire internal access to its models and systems ( OpenAI ). 
Scope by group : Apollo places six evaluators onsite for four months ( Rundown ). METR reviews OpenAI's largest RL run, with access to transcripts, monitor records and checkpoint snapshots ( METR ). Transluce runs a six-week audit of post-training alignment evals, with a fuller follow-up in early 2027 ( Transluce ). Goodfire embeds interpretability researchers to monitor training runs ( Goodfire ). 
Limits : METR says its scope excludes the misalignment incidents OpenAI has disclosed and is narrower than METR proposed ( scope ). 
Criticism of the access terms : Critics say the deals fall short of Sam Altman's promise of "employee-like access." 
Reported gaps : Assessors get no Slack access, OpenAI selects which staff they interview, and they cannot access weights or run training-based elicitation ( Neel Nanda , Alex Mallen ). 
Former-employee account : Mikita Balesni says assessors cannot quote employees, even anonymously, and some may be barred from publishing on internal-only models ( balesni ). 
Goodfire acquisition talks : The Information reports OpenAI explored buying the interpretability startup for more than $5B. Goodfire reportedly wanted to stay independent so it could sell to multiple labs ( report ). 
Other integrity signals : 
Benchmark contamination : Claude appears to have memorized details of the LinuxArena control eval ( Karvonen ). 
Incident taxonomy : OpenAI published a v0.1 framework for classifying AI control incidents ( framework ). 
Disclosure policy : Anthropic is cutting its coordinated disclosure window from 90 to 30 days for high- and critical-severity vulnerabilities ( policy ). 
Inference systems and agent infrastructure 
Together moves on from hand-tuned megakernels. Its first design made it into production for one customer. Agents now search for smaller groups of GPU operations to fuse. Together reports 28% higher throughput on Llama 3.2 1B on B200. Engineering writeup 
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on Vera Rubin : vLLM with Dynamo on SemiAnalysis's AgentX benchmark shows 63.4x per-chip throughput over GB300 NVL72 at 400 tok/s/user, and 93.3x at 600 ( vLLM ). 
Batch-1 latency : SGLang-adjacent work reaches ~2,500 tok/s at batch size 1 on TP4, 1.7x its GB300 result ( saltyph ). Baseten reports a similar 1.7x over its 4xB300 numbers ( Baseten ). 
Agent-driven optimization : An agent
d Engram tables across HBM via NVLink symmetric memory to recover prefix-cache capacity ( Liu ). Another team says agents found optimizations that made its B300 step time 10% faster ( Halex ). 
Agentic serving research : MIT's Evolving Infra replaces fixed prefill/decode disaggregation with online adaptation. Against NVIDIA Dynamo on up to 256 GB300s, it reports up to 4.1x lower latency and 14x lower P95 TTFT ( Evolving Infra ). 
Pipeline-parallel prefill : Inferact finds PP2 on MiniMax-M3.1-Flash sustains 23% more requests per GPU than DEP2 at a 2s TTFT target ( Inferact ). 
Prefix-cache pitfalls : Ollama found that a single system-prompt timestamp or a change in reasoning effort can wipe the cache ( Ollama ). 
Sandboxes and training : 
External sandboxes : Simon Willison describes running agents on a Mac while executing their code in WebAssembly, QEMU or Apple Container sandboxes. The pattern includes allow-list proxies and credential replacement ( post ). 
MLPerf : In MLPerf Training v6.1, a GB300 NVL72 trained GPT-OSS-20B in 19.7 minutes, 2.86x faster than H100 ( Lambda ).

PyBot : A swarm of 1,000 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash agents spent a week writing a rule-based chatbot with no neural network ( lewtun ). 
Scale : The agents exchanged ~175k messages and merged ~8k PRs. 
Result : The bot is 630k lines of Python with zero dependencies and is reported on par with SmolLM-360M on everyday questions. 
Self-improvement and training : 
AutoRL : Agents supervising a live RL run lifted Qwen3 on AIME 2024 from 46.67% to 66.67% ( omarsar0 ). 
Benchmark-gaming caveat : A roundup warns that many self-improving agent gains come from learning the benchmark rather than the task ( TuringPost ). 
Weight-space programming : Opus 5.5 hand-wrote transformer weights that solved algorithmic tasks with a median of 166 parameters ( dair_ai ). 
Data curation : DatologyAI published the tech report behind its claimed 6x pretraining compute multiplier ( Datology ). 
Distillation reproduction : A small-scale replication confirms perturbed-input distillation helps when the student trains from scratch, but finds it hurts when distilling into a pretrained student ( Maini ). 
New benchmarks : 
GradeBench : The best frontier model agrees with instructors only 57% of the time when grading handwritten physics answers ( GradeBench ). 
Time to First Audio : AA's new TTS latency benchmark finds a median of 376 ms for streaming models versus 2.0 s for non-streaming ones ( AA ). 
SpeedRunBench : Inkling-2-Small cleared SuperTux 1-1 in 1,988 frames, ahead of Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol ( SpeedRunBench ). 
Science models and developer tools 
Gemini 4 Carbon : DeepMind says Carbon powered AlphaProof Code agents that verified Signal's cryptographic code. It also spotted wet-lab errors and found 40x more related protein sequences ( details ). 
Science access : Google expanded free Carbon access for 10,000 scientists through Antigravity ( program ). 
Context window : Antigravity doubled the context window for Argon, Carbon and Hydrogen, cutting compaction 3.5x per user turn ( Mohan ). 
User reports (anecdotal) : One researcher says Carbon solved a problem that waves of Astra and Fable attempts had not ( anecdote ). 
OpenAI for science and health : OpenAI is opening free frontier access to up to 200,000 scientists, with applications from Nov 23 ( program ). 
Productivity study : OpenAI reports scientists roughly doubled their productivity in a study of 1,800 participants ( study ). 
Physics showcase : Physicist Nathaniel Craig used GPT-6 Astra to develop a candidate lattice definition of the Standard Model ( blog ). 
Healthcare : ChatGPT for Healthcare adds computer-use agents and more than 20 plugins ( healthcare ). 
Claude Code : The desktop app now runs iPhone Duo in the iOS simulator and can fold and unfold the device to test layouts ( ClaudeDevs ). 
Verification : The team published how it uses cheap tests, benchmarks and end-to-end runs to let Claude verify its own work ( blog ). 
Unreleased model (unconfirmed) : A "Silicon 2" entry spotted in Devin is suspected to be an Anthropic model ( rumor ). 
Liquid d1.2-ultra : It ranks #1 on AA's Decision Index at $0.042 per M input tokens ( AA ). 
Sage S2.1 Flash : The open-weight science model reports leading MLE-bench Lite and OfficeQA Pro results ( Sage ). 
FLUX-mimic-x : A 7B video-action robotics model ranks #1 on RoboLab among real-time models ( mimic ). 
Unsloth computer use : Local models can now drive desktop apps and game engines through Unsloth ( Unsloth ). 
Industry and policy 
Nvidia. The US Commerce and Justice departments issued a joint statement on the Megaspeed investigation. Commerce 
Financing and M&A : 
Noeri : Yejin Choi and Carlos Guestrin's continual-learning lab raised $110M ( Choi ). 
Corma : The cyber-defense model company raised a $125M Series A at a $1B valuation ( Corma ). 
World Labs : The team is joining AMD ( Fei-Fei Li ). 
Market data : Anthropic's S-1 shows $16.3B revenue in H1 2026 and compute costs falling from 251% to 48% of revenue ( The Batch ). 
Enterprise adoption : Databricks reports open-model token
rose from 7.3% to 30.9% in 3.5 months ( summary ). 
AI Reddit Recap 
Local models and hardware 
What fits in 16 GB? Unsloth expects a smaller Qwen4-27B to run in 16 GB. Local users want to see the quantization and how much memory is left for the context window. One developer already splits coding jobs between Opus for specs and a local Qwen3.8-27B for implementation. Memory discussion · Local workflows 
Hy4 Flash. Tencent’s multimodal model has 224B parameters and activates 12B per token. At $0.070 per million input tokens and $0.281 per million output tokens, it gives developers a cheaper way to try Hy4’s 1M context window. Tencent’s release · Discussion 
EUROPA. A reported test run on the JUPITER supercomputer trained a roughly 952B-parameter mixture of experts with 32.8B parameters active per token. The local-model community’s question is why the team chose that scale for its first model. Training run and discussion 
Where do two quantizations diverge? inside-llm loads two GGUFs with the same tokenizer and lets you step through their predictions side by side. Watch the first token where they disagree, then compare the probabilities they assigned to the alternatives. Project · Demo and discussion 
Basalt’s 770 tokens/sec headline depends on what you generate. The developer reports up to 776 tokens/sec for structured output from Qwen3.8-27B, 262 in chat and 194 for prose. Readers asked for longer quality tests of the 4-bit prefill. Basalt · Benchmark thread 
An FPGA running Qwen 27B. Valley Semiconductor reports 7.9 tokens/sec on short prompts and about 5.5 in live chat. Its 50 tokens/sec target at 20 W is a projection for a future chip. Live demo · Hardware discussion 
Agents in use 
Claude Meetings. A CTO describes inviting Claude into a 30-minute Google Meet. It updated project records in Notion and called the team’s own tools to update bids during the meeting. Field report 
A Minecraft test for Hydrogen. A developer asked Gemini 4 Hydrogen to recover missing source and build a datapack for 11 Minecraft versions. The agent reportedly launched two graphical clients to test fixes for dropped items and raycasts. Developer’s account 
What teams hire a harness developer to do. One example from the discussion: a coding agent can propose a change, while the harness decides which repository it may write to, which CI test counts as passing and when a person needs to approve the next step. Claude Code discussion 
Vision and video 
Testing a video model’s physics. After a second MiniMax H3 demo, commenters proposed a harder test: describe the scene, leave the outcome out of the prompt and see whether the model predicts what the objects will do. Demo and discussion
